q1_issues.issue: "could" is encoded as a bare (Can ...) with no Past; the instruction set licenses only Can/Permitted plus Past for the past-narrative reading, or Might with no tense for the speculative one.
"known as a 'poison pill'" is flattened into a bare type atom, dropping the naming predication that a participial post-modifier is required to reify as a reduced-relative event.

"undesired suitors" is fused into undesired_suitor although "undesired" is a descriptive modifier that passes the predication test - fusion is reserved for classifying modifiers, and no modifier genus is emitted for it either.

q2_gaps: an appellation predicate "known as / called <common-noun label>" - there is no carrier for an alias that is not a proper noun, since Name is reserved for proper nouns
a bare-plural object inside a non-finite purpose clause carrying a descriptive modifier - the bare-kind-filler route has no slot for the modifier and the distributive plural route needs a witness
notes: The proper-noun premodifier ("PeopleSoft management") correctly takes Possession, "choose to activate" correctly takes the tenseless top-level control-complement pattern with subject control, and "designed to thwart" is a correct tenseless reduced relative with the purpose To. poison_pill correctly gets no pill genus.
